name: SnapOtter
description: Self-hosted file toolkit with 200+ tools for image, video, audio, PDF, and file workflows. SnapOtter keeps files on your Unraid server and includes an image editor, batch jobs, pipelines, REST API access, OIDC/SSO support, and optional local AI features.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Persistent SnapOtter data, including embedded PostgreSQL and Redis data, files, logs, settings, AI models, and installed AI bundles.

paths.name: Workspace
paths.description: Temporary processing workspace. SnapOtter cleans job data automatically, but this path should have enough free space for large media and batch operations.

ports.name: WebUI
ports.description: HTTP port for the SnapOtter web interface.

variables.name: AUTH_ENABLED
variables.description: Require login for the web UI and API. Leave enabled unless SnapOtter is protected by another trusted authentication layer.

variables.name: DEFAULT_USERNAME
variables.description: Initial admin username. Used only when the first admin account is created.

variables.name: DEFAULT_PASSWORD
variables.description: Initial admin password. Change it after first login.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID for files created in mounted paths. Unraid's nobody user is usually 99.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID for files created in mounted paths. Unraid's users group is usually 100.

variables.name: MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB
variables.description: Maximum upload size per file in MB. Set to 0 for unlimited.

variables.name: MAX_BATCH_SIZE
variables.description: Maximum number of files in a batch. Set to 0 for unlimited.

variables.name: CONCURRENT_JOBS
variables.description: Number of batch jobs to process in parallel. Set to 0 to auto-detect from CPU cores.

variables.name: REDIS_MAXMEMORY
variables.description: Memory cap for embedded Redis. Lower this on memory-constrained systems.

variables.name: TRUST_PROXY
variables.description: Trust X-Forwarded-For headers from a reverse proxy. Set to false if SnapOtter is not behind a trusted proxy.
